section.title: Modeling Forces in the Real World
Modeling Forces in the Real World

items.primary_i_can: I can draw a force diagram for an object in a real-world situation.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.5: construct/critique real-world force models, balanced/unbalanced classification, net-force-to-motion explanation.
items.student_text: A backpack hangs motionless from one strap. Draw a force diagram for the backpack only.
items.student_html: A backpack hangs motionless from one strap. Draw a force diagram for the backpack only.
items.answer: upward strap tension and downward weight, equal in magnitude
items.solution_text: Only forces acting on the backpack belong in its diagram; motionless means the vertical forces balance.
items.solution_html: Only forces acting on the backpack belong in its diagram; motionless means the vertical forces balance.

section.title: Modeling Forces in the Real World

items.primary_i_can: I can draw a force diagram for an object in a real-world situation.
items.evidence_job: Critique forces on the wrong object or missing interactions.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.5: construct/critique real-world force models, balanced/unbalanced classification, net-force-to-motion explanation.
items.student_text: Candidate diagram for a book on a table includes: weight on book downward, table support on book upward, and “book pushes table downward.” What is wrong?
items.student_html: Candidate diagram for a book on a table includes: weight on book downward, table support on book upward, and “book pushes table downward.” What is wrong?
items.answer: The force the book exerts on the table acts on the table, not on the book, so it does not belong in the book’s force diagram.
items.solution_text: A free-body diagram contains only forces acting on the chosen object.
items.solution_html: A free-body diagram contains only forces acting on the chosen object.

section.title: Modeling Forces in the Real World

items.primary_i_can: I can decide whether the forces are balanced or unbalanced.

items.student_text:
Rank these models from smallest to largest net-force magnitude:
A: 20 N ← [box] → 20 N
B: 10 N ← [box] → 25 N
C: 40 N ← [box] → 15 N
items.student_html:
Rank these models from smallest to largest net-force magnitude:
A: 20 N ← [box] → 20 N
B: 10 N ← [box] → 25 N
C: 40 N ← [box] → 15 N
items.solution_text: A has 0 N, B has 15 N, and C has 25 N net-force magnitude.
items.solution_html: A has 0 N, B has 15 N, and C has 25 N net-force magnitude.

section.title: Modeling Forces in the Real World

items.primary_i_can: I can decide whether the forces are balanced or unbalanced.
items.evidence_job: Use net force to classify the model’s balance.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.5: construct/critique real-world force models, balanced/unbalanced classification, net-force-to-motion explanation.
items.student_text: A cart has 48 N right and 31 N left. Find the net force and classify the horizontal forces as balanced or unbalanced.
items.student_html: A cart has 48 N right and 31 N left. Find the net force and classify the horizontal forces as balanced or unbalanced.
items.solution_text: 48 − 31 = 17 N right. A nonzero result means the forces are unbalanced.
items.solution_html: 48 − 31 = 17 N right. A nonzero result means the forces are unbalanced.

section.title: Modeling Forces in the Real World

items.primary_i_can: I can explain how the net force affects the object’s motion and critique an incorrect force explanation and revise it using physics vocabulary.
items.evidence_job: Revise an incorrect force explanation using physics vocabulary.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.5: construct/critique real-world force models, balanced/unbalanced classification, net-force-to-motion explanation.
items.student_text: A student says, “The box is moving left, so the net force must point left.” The box is slowing down. Revise the explanation.
items.student_html: A student says, “The box is moving left, so the net force must point left.” The box is slowing down. Revise the explanation.
items.answer: If the box is moving left and slowing, its velocity is changing to the right, so the net force points right.
items.solution_text: Net force aligns with change in velocity, not necessarily the current direction of motion.
items.solution_html: Net force aligns with change in velocity, not necessarily the current direction of motion.

section.title: Modeling Forces in the Real World

items.primary_i_can: I can explain how the net force affects the object’s motion and critique an incorrect force explanation and revise it using physics vocabulary.
items.evidence_job: Connect net force shown by a model to observed motion change.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.5: construct/critique real-world force models, balanced/unbalanced classification, net-force-to-motion explanation.
items.student_text: Observed motion: a cart is speeding up right. Model: 30 N ← [cart] → 45 N. Are the model and motion evidence consistent? Explain.
items.student_html: Observed motion: a cart is speeding up right. Model: 30 N ← [cart] → 45 N. Are the model and motion evidence consistent? Explain.
items.answer: Yes; the net force is 15 N right, matching a rightward change in velocity.
items.solution_text: The rightward force exceeds the leftward force, so the model predicts a rightward motion change.
items.solution_html: The rightward force exceeds the leftward force, so the model predicts a rightward motion change.
